<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="31" type="chapter">
                  <ns0:head>CHAP. XXXI.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p n="1">1 AND the LORD spake unto Moses, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 See I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">He seems to be the same mentioned 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 2. 20.</ns0:note> of the tribe of Judah.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And I have filled him with the spirit of God<ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Which was now necessary, because the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> wanted ingenuous education to learn these things, and therefore needed inspiration.</ns0:note>, in <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>with,</ns0:hi> the following clauses being ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plicatory of the former, shewing what gifts of the spirit God had filled him with, to wit, Wisdom, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> wisdom, and in understanding, and in know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge, and in all manner of workmanship.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:78" />4 To devise cunning works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 And in cutting of stones, to set <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> and in carving of timber, to work in all manner of workmanship.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And I, behold, I have given with him, A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />holiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan: and in the hearts of all that are wise-hearted <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">That have wisdom and skil sufficient to do these things under the inspection and direction of <ns0:hi>Bezaleel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Aholiab,</ns0:hi> the principal workmen.</ns0:note> I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 The tabernacle of the congregation, and the ark of the testimony, and the mercy-seat that is thereupon, and all the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> vessel.</ns0:note> furniture of the taber<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nacle:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And the table, and his furniture, and the pure candlestick, with all his furniture, and the altar of incense:<ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">So called by way of eminency, not onely because it was made of pure gold, and was not defiled with blood, for so some other things were, but especially to mind the Priests of their du<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty in keeping it neat and clean, it being more subject to defile<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment than other things.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 And the altar of burnt-offering, with all his furniture, and the laver and his foot:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>h. 39. 1. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> the clothes of service <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Wherein the Ark and other sacred utensils were wrapped up when they were to be removed. See <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 35. 19. and <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 4.</ns0:note>, and the ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly garments for Aaron the priest, and the gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments of his sons, to minister in the priests office:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And the anointing oil, and <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> incense of <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> sweet in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cense for the holy <ns0:hi>place:</ns0:hi> according to all that I have commanded thee shall they do.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And the LORD spake unto Moses, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, saying, Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">This precept is here repeated, either 1. to shew the chief use of the Tabernacle and all this cost and trouble about it, to wit, that they might there acceptably serve God, as in some measure upon every day, so especially upon the Sabbath day. Or rather 2. to restrain the time for the doing of the fore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mentioned works, <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Though the work of the Tabernacle and utensils be holy and for an holy use, yet I will not have it done upon my holy day. The sabbath was not made for them, but they for it, and therefore they shall give place to it.</ns0:note>: for it <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> a sign between me and you <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The sabbath is a fivefold sign, 1. Commemorative, of Gods crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of and Dominion over them and all other things, to whom they do hereby profess their subjection. 2. Indicative, shew<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing that they were made to be holy, and that their sanctifica<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion can be had from none but from God, as it here follows, and from the observation of Gods days and appointments. 3. Distinctive, whereby they owned themselves to be the Lords peculiar people by a religious keeping of those Sabbaths, which the rest of the World grossely neglected and profanely scossed a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>. 4. Pr<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>figurative of that rest which Christ should purchase for them, to wit, a rest from the burden of the cere<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monial, and from the cur<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s and rigours of the moral, Law, as also from s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n and the wrath of God for ever. See <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 4. 5. Confirmative, both assuring them of Gods good will to them, and that as he blessed the Sabbath for their sakes so he would bless them in the holy use of it with temporal, spiritual and e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verlasting blessings, as he declares in many places of Scripture, and assuring God of their standing to that covenant made be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tween God and them. So that this was a mutual stipulation or ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tification of the covenant of grace on both sides.</ns0:note>, throughout your generations, that ye may know that I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> the LORD that doth sanctifie you <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">That selecteth you out of all people and consecrate you to my self and to my service and worship, a great part whereof is the observation of the Sabbath. Or, that sanctifieth you by my Word and Ordi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nances, which are in more eminent and solemn manner dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pensed upon the Sabbath day, by the observation whereof you declare that you own me as your onely sanctifier. And so we may observe, the sabbath owns the Lord as our Creatour and as our Redeemer and as our Sanctifier, and therefore it is no wonder God so severely enjoyns the sanctification of the Sab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bath and punisheth the neglect of it, it being a tacit renounc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing or disowning of God the Father, the Son, and the holy Ghost.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 20. 8. Deut. 5. 12. Ezek. 20. 12.</ns0:note> Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore: for it <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> holy unto you: every one that desileth it, shall surely be put to death <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Of which see an example <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 15. 32. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 15. 35.</ns0:note> whosoever doth <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> work <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Servile work, as it is explained, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 23. 7. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> therein, that soul shall be cut off from amongst his people.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 Six days <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> shall be done.</ns0:note> may work be done, but in the seventh <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the sabbath of rest <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>the sabbath of sabbaths,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>of sabbaths, i. e.</ns0:hi> the great and chief sabbath, as <ns0:hi>the song of songs</ns0:hi> is the most excellent song, <ns0:hi>the holy of holies</ns0:hi> is the most holy, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had many sabbaths or days of rest, but this is here preferred before them all by this emphatical repetition of the same word, and by this argument the foregoing duty is pressed upon them.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> holiness.</ns0:note> holy to the LORD: whosoever doeth <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> work in the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>shall keep the sabbath by observing</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>celebrating the sabbath, i. e.</ns0:hi> by observing or celebrating it, the antecedent being put for the relative, as is frequently done. So here is another most emphatical repetition to oblige us to the greater caution and diligence in this great duty, and to shew what stress God lays upon it, who hath therefore placed this in the midst of the commands of the Decalogue, as the heart which gives life and vigour to all the rest. Or it may be rendered thus, <ns0:hi>shall observe the day of rest to celebrate the sabbath,</ns0:hi> and so the phrase is like that, in the 4th. Command, <ns0:hi>Remember the sabbath day to keep it holy.</ns0:hi> So here, <ns0:hi>Observe the sabbath, i. e.</ns0:hi> watch its coming and approach, consider attentively the nature and use of it, and that not as a matter of idle speculation, but of serious practise, or so <ns0:hi>that you may do</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>celebrate the Sabbath, i. e.</ns0:hi> perform all the duties of it. Or thus, <ns0:hi>shall observe the sabbath, to make</ns0:hi> it <ns0:hi>a sabbath,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>day of rest,</ns0:hi> and that no idle or carnal rest, but <ns0:hi>a rest, holy to the Lord,</ns0:hi> as it is called in the foregoing verse.</ns0:note> throughout their generations <ns0:hi>for</ns0:hi> a perpetual covenant <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Or, by <ns0:hi>a perpetual covenant:</ns0:hi> or, it is <ns0:hi>a perpetual covenant, i. e.</ns0:hi> condition or part of that agree<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment made between me and them, they have solemnly cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nanted or promised that they will do all that I commanded them, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 24. 7, 8, among which this is a chief branch, and I have covenanted to bless and sanctify them in so doing. And this word <ns0:hi>perpetual,</ns0:hi> as also the word <ns0:hi>for ever</ns0:hi> being added to it in the next verse, may intimate that this hath a longer perpetuity than the c<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
